question: Which of the following is one of the basic vehicle control skills maneuvers illustrated in the manual's Section 12 figures?
choice_a: Student Discharge
choice_b: Railroad Crossing Stop
choice_c: Expressway Merging
choice_d: Straight Line Backing
explanation: Section 12 shows the Basic Control Skills Test maneuvers, including Figure 12.1: Straight Line Backing, along with offset backing, parallel parking, and alley dock. Expressway merging, railroad crossings, and student discharge are covered in Section 13's on-road driving test.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test

question: According to the Basic Control Skills Test figures, the offset backing maneuver is tested in which two directions?
choice_a: Forward and reverse
choice_b: Uphill and downhill
choice_c: Right and left
choice_d: Driver side and passenger side only
explanation: The manual illustrates Figure 12.2: Offset Back/Right and Figure 12.3: Offset Back/Left as the two offset backing maneuvers in the Basic Control Skills Test.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test

question: Which Basic Control Skills Test maneuver requires backing your vehicle into a dock area, illustrated at a 90-degree angle in the manual?
choice_a: Offset Back/Right
choice_b: Straight Line Backing
choice_c: Alley Dock
choice_d: Urban Business
explanation: Figure 12.6 depicts the Alley Dock maneuver, shown as a 90-degree Alley Dock, which requires backing the vehicle into a dock space.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test

question: During the on-road driving test, which of the following is a requirement you must meet at all times?
choice_a: Wear your safety belt
choice_b: Keep the radio off
choice_c: Drive at the posted speed limit regardless of traffic conditions
choice_d: Use the horn at every intersection
explanation: The manual states that at all times during the on-road test you must drive in a safe and responsible manner, wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, How You Will Be Tested

question: If your test route does not include a certain traffic situation, such as a railroad crossing, what may the examiner ask you to do instead?
choice_a: Reschedule the test for another day
choice_b: Automatically fail that section
choice_c: Simulate the traffic situation by explaining what you are or would be doing
choice_d: Skip that portion of the test entirely with no penalty
explanation: The manual explains that if the test route does not have certain traffic situations, you may be asked to simulate them by telling the examiner what you are or would be doing if you were in that traffic situation.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, How You Will Be Tested

question: According to the manual, unsafe coasting occurs when your vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for how long?
choice_a: More than the length of your vehicle
choice_b: At any time while approaching a turn
choice_c: More than 100 feet
choice_d: More than 30 seconds
explanation: The manual defines unsafe coasting as occurring when your vehicle is out of gear for more than the length of your vehicle while slowing down for a turn.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 13.1.1 - Turns

question: If you are stopping behind another vehicle during the on-road test, where should you stop to maintain a safe gap?
choice_a: As close as possible to the vehicle ahead
choice_b: At least one full block behind the vehicle ahead
choice_c: Only when the vehicle ahead has come to a complete stop for at least 10 seconds
choice_d: Where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you
explanation: The manual instructs that if stopping behind another vehicle, you should stop where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you, which represents a safe gap, and your vehicle must not roll.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 13.1.1 - Turns

question: While driving through an intersection during the on-road test, what must you avoid doing?
choice_a: Checking traffic thoroughly in all directions
choice_b: Keeping your hands on the wheel
choice_c: Changing lanes while proceeding through the intersection
choice_d: Yielding to pedestrians in the intersection
explanation: The manual states that when driving through an intersection, you must not change lanes while proceeding through the intersection, must check traffic thoroughly, yield to pedestrians and traffic, and keep your hands on the wheel.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 13.1.2 - Intersections

question: As you approach an intersection with a stop sign, what must you do regarding coasting?
choice_a: Come to a complete stop with no coasting, maintaining a safe gap behind any vehicle in front of you
choice_b: Coast through if no other vehicles are visible
choice_c: Slow to a rolling stop only
choice_d: Coast up to the stop line to save fuel
explanation: The manual specifies that as you approach an intersection, if necessary, you must come to a complete stop (no coasting) behind any stop signs, signals, sidewalks, or stop lines, maintaining a safe gap, and your vehicle must not roll forward or backward.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 13.1.2 - Intersections

question: During the Urban Business portion of the on-road test, where should your vehicle be positioned?
choice_a: As close to the center line as possible
choice_b: Centered in the proper lane, which is the right-most lane
choice_c: Straddling two lanes to allow for merging
choice_d: Centered in the left-most lane at all times
explanation: The manual states that during Urban Business driving, your vehicle should be centered in the proper lane (right-most lane), and you should keep up with the flow of traffic but not exceed the posted speed limit.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 13.1.3 - Urban Business

question: Before entering an expressway, what should you do?
choice_a: Stop at the on-ramp until traffic clears completely
choice_b: Enter without signaling to avoid confusing other drivers
choice_c: Accelerate to maximum speed before merging
choice_d: Check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane
explanation: The manual instructs that before entering the expressway, you should check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane of traffic.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 13.1.5 - Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: During the Stop/Start maneuver, once your vehicle is stopped, what should you do with the parking brake and gear shift?
choice_a: Shift into reverse and apply the parking brake
choice_b: Apply the parking brake and move the gear shift to neutral or park
choice_c: Apply the parking brake but keep your foot on the clutch
choice_d: Leave the parking brake off and keep the vehicle in gear
explanation: The manual states that once stopped for the Stop/Start maneuver, you should activate your four-way emergency flashers, apply the parking brake, move the gear shift to neutral or park, and remove your feet from the brake and clutch pedals.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 13.1.6 - Stop/Start

question: When resuming from the Stop/Start maneuver and releasing the parking brake, what should you NOT do before the vehicle begins to move?
choice_a: Activate the left turn signal
choice_b: Turn off the four-way flashers
choice_c: Check traffic in all directions
choice_d: Turn the steering wheel
explanation: The manual instructs that when resuming, you should release the parking brake and pull straight ahead, and you must not turn the wheel before your vehicle moves.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 13.1.6 - Stop/Start

question: When approaching a curve during the on-road test, what should you do before entering it?
choice_a: Reduce speed so that further braking or shifting is not required in the curve
choice_b: Shift into neutral to coast through the curve
choice_c: Accelerate to maintain momentum through the curve
choice_d: Brake heavily while turning the steering wheel
explanation: The manual states that before entering a curve, you should reduce speed so that further braking or shifting is not required in the curve, and you should keep the vehicle in the lane.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 13.1.7 - Curve

question: While any part of your vehicle is in a railroad crossing, what must you NOT do?
choice_a: Keep your hands on the steering wheel
choice_b: Stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes
choice_c: Look and listen for trains
choice_d: Continue moving forward at a steady speed
explanation: The manual states that you must not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is in a railroad crossing.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 13.1.8 - Railroad Crossing

question: If you are driving a bus, school bus, or a vehicle displaying placards, the manual requires you to stop at a railroad crossing within how many feet, but not less than how many feet, from the nearest rail?
choice_a: Within 15 feet, but not less than 5 feet
choice_b: Within 50 feet, but not less than 15 feet
choice_c: Within 25 feet, but not less than 5 feet
choice_d: Within 100 feet, but not less than 25 feet
explanation: The manual states that vehicles required to stop at railroad crossings (buses, school buses, placarded vehicles) must stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 13.1.8 - Railroad Crossing

question: After driving under an overpass during the on-road test, what might the examiner ask you to identify?
choice_a: The name of the overpass
choice_b: The speed limit under the overpass
choice_c: The posted clearance or height
choice_d: The posted weight limit
explanation: The manual states that after driving under an overpass, you may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted clearance or height was; after going over a bridge, you may be asked about the posted weight limit.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 13.1.9 - Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: For a School Bus endorsement, the manual requires the school bus to come to a complete stop how far away from students at the stop before student discharge begins?
choice_a: At least 25 feet away
choice_b: At least 10 feet away
choice_c: At least 50 feet away
choice_d: At least 5 feet away
explanation: The manual states that when stopping for student discharge, you must bring the school bus to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students at the stop, place the transmission in neutral/park, set the parking brake, and activate the stop arm and red warning lights.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 13.1.10 - Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: As a school bus approaches a student pick up, what warning lights and signals must be activated?
choice_a: Amber warning lights and the right turn signal
choice_b: High beam headlights
choice_c: Red warning lights and the left turn signal
choice_d: Only the hazard flashers
explanation: The manual states that as you approach the student pick up, you must decelerate, continue checking traffic, activate amber warning lights and right turn signals, and move as far as possible to the right on the traveled portion of the roadway.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 13.1.10 - Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: Regarding clutch usage on a manual transmission vehicle, which practice does the manual warn against?
choice_a: Riding the clutch to control speed, coasting with the clutch depressed, or "popping" the clutch
choice_b: Double-clutching on an unsynchronized transmission
choice_c: Always using the clutch to shift
choice_d: Avoiding revving or lugging the engine
explanation: The manual states that under Clutch Usage, you should always use the clutch to shift and double-clutch if the transmission is unsynchronized, but you must not ride the clutch to control speed, coast with the clutch depressed, or "pop" the clutch.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 13.1.11(a) - Clutch Usage

question: Under the Gear Usage general driving behavior category, when should you avoid shifting gears?
choice_a: On straight, empty roads
choice_b: While on the expressway
choice_c: In turns and intersections
choice_d: While approaching a stop sign
explanation: The manual states that under Gear Usage, you should not grind or clash gears, should select a gear that does not rev or lug the engine, and should not shift in turns and intersections.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 13.1.12(b) - Gear Usage

question: Under the Brake Usage general driving behavior category, how should you apply the brakes?
choice_a: By riding the brake lightly at all times for readiness
choice_b: As harshly as possible in all stopping situations
choice_c: By pumping the brake repeatedly for better control
choice_d: Smoothly, using steady pressure, without riding or pumping the brake
explanation: The manual states that under Brake Usage, you should not ride or pump the brake and should not brake harshly, but instead brake smoothly using steady pressure.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 13.1.13(c) - Brake Usage

question: Under the Lane Usage category, on a multiple lane road, in which lane should you finish a left turn?
choice_a: The right-most (curb) lane
choice_b: Any lane that is open
choice_c: The lane directly to the right of the center line
choice_d: The lane farthest from the center line
explanation: The manual states that under Lane Usage, you should complete a turn in the proper lane on a multiple lane road, with the vehicle finishing a left turn in the lane directly to the right of the center line, and finishing a right turn in the right-most (curb) lane.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 13.1.14(d) - Lane Usage

question: Under the Use of Turn Signals category, when should you cancel your turn signal?
choice_a: Turn signals should never be cancelled manually
choice_b: Upon completion of a turn or lane change
choice_c: Only when the examiner instructs you to
choice_d: Before beginning the turn
explanation: The manual states that you should use turn signals properly, activate them when required and at appropriate times, and cancel turn signals upon completion of a turn or lane change.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 13.1.17 - Use of Turn Signals
